Notice that, by continuity, this is still true if σ1,..., σn are independent almost everywhere on L. In particular, the singularities of L will be completely determined by the singularities of the smooth map Phi = ( σ1,..., σn): M → Rn. However, the singularities of Phi must be very special. artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed (compact, without boundary) two-dimensional real analytic surface. A (1,1)-tensor field $L$ on $M$ is called a Nijenhuis operator if its Nijenhuis torsion
$$N_L(X,Y) = L^2[X,Y] - L[LX,Y] - L[X,LY] + [LX,LY]$$
vanishes identically for all smooth vector fields $X, Y$ on $M$.

Construct real analytic examples of Nijenhuis operators $L$ on a closed two-dimensional surface $M$ such that:
(i) at every point of $M$ the two eigenvalues of $L$ are real, and
(ii) on an open dense subset of $M$ the two eigenvalues are distinct.

Equivalently, determine on which closed real analytic surfaces such operators exist and exhibit explicit constructions of them.

(For context: if $\chi(t) = \det(t\cdot\mathrm{Id} - L) = t^2 + \sigma_1(x)t + \sigma_2(x)$ is the characteristic polynomial of $L$, then in local coordinates $(x,y)$ in which $\sigma_1 = x$ and $\sigma_2 = f(x,y)$, the Nijenhuis condition at points where $d\sigma_1, d\sigma_2$ are linearly dependent with $d\Phi$ of rank one forces
$$L = \begin{pmatrix} f_x - x & f_y \\ f_x(x - f_x) - f & -f_x \end{pmatrix},$$
so that admissibility of $\sigma_2 = f$ requires $\frac{f_x(x - f_x) - f}{f_y}$ to extend as a smooth function. The problem asks for global real analytic realizations of such structures.)
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on Nijenhuis geometry in dimension 2 (e.g., a 2025 preprint on singularities of two-dimensional Nijenhuis operators) addresses related questions (Problem 5.13 on admissible discriminants) but does not construct global real analytic examples on closed surfaces with real, generically distinct eigenvalues. Related results on gl-regular Nijenhuis operators give topological obstructions, but the explicit construction problem on closed surfaces appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Singularities of two-dimensional Nijenhuis operators
status_evidence.snippet: The paper addresses Problem 5.13 from Bolsinov et al., providing local constructions in neighborhoods of the origin in R^2, not on closed surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Recent 2025 work on 2D Nijenhuis operators is local and addresses a different problem (5.13), not the global construction on closed surfaces.

status_evidence.title: Nijenhuis Geometry III: gl-regular Nijenhuis operators
status_evidence.snippet: Theorem 1.3 provides topological obstructions for existence of regular Nijenhuis operators on closed two-dimensional surfaces.
status_evidence.claim: Topological obstructions are known but explicit real analytic global examples with real, generically distinct eigenvalues are not constructed.
